findings.title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, deletions not awaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ...}) does not wait for the async callbacks. forEach ignores returned promises, so Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting complete. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks, causing unhandled rejections and leaving external calendar/video events undeleted, keeping old time blocked.

findings.title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, deletions not awaited
findings.body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ...}) does not wait for the async callbacks. forEach discards the promises, so the function returns before calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting finish. Errors inside become unhandled rejections not caught by the surrounding try/catch, leaving stale external events and incorrect availability.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletions fired without awaiting
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ... calendar.deleteEvent ... deleteMeeting ...}) is not awaited. The mutation sends the reschedule email and returns while deletions are still in flight. Failures are unhandled rejections with no logging, so old calendar/video events can remain and the previous slot is not freed.

findings.title: Recurring cancel pushes to apiDeletes from unawaited forEach
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }) populates apiDeletes asynchronously. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) snapshots apiDeletes before the async callbacks have pushed, so recurring-booking cancellations do not wait for external calendar deletions. On serverless the background work can be killed, leaving ghost events on Google/Office calendars and inconsistent state.

findings.title: Video adapters loaded sequentially instead of in parallel
findings.body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts line 24 getVideoAdapters loops for (const cred of withCredentials) { await appStore[...] } awaiting each dynamic import one by one. Previously adapter creation was synchronous. With multiple video credentials this serializes module loads and slows getBusyVideoTimes/createMeeting/updateMeeting. It should use Promise.all to load in parallel.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are eager, not lazy
findings.body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the object is built as { applecalendar: import('./applecalendar'), ... }. Each import() executes immediately when the module is first imported, so all 29 apps start loading upfront. This defeats lazy code-splitting, retains the startup cost the PR intended to remove, and creates long-lived rejected promises if any app fails to load instead of loading on demand.

findings.title: Dynamic import rejection not handled, breaks availability
findings.body: In packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts line 15 await appStore[...] can reject if the dynamic import fails. There is no try/catch, so getCalendar now rejects instead of returning null with a warning. Callers like getCachedResults do await Promise.all(credentials.map(getCalendar)) with no handling, so one broken app import fails the entire availability fetch for a booking page rather than skipping that calendar.
